prompt: Storybook painterly illustration, night, HIGH CONTRAST with deep true blacks. A MINIATURE VILLAGE BUILT BY CAT-SIZED CREATURES — the whole settlement is tiny, and its scale is shown by NATURE TOWERING OVER IT: fern fronds arch higher than the rooflines, blades of grass rise past the eaves, a fallen pine cone beside the lane is larger than a barrel, mushroom caps stand as tall as the doorways, moss grows like shrubbery, dewdrops are heavy and huge on the leaves. The buildings are small and beautifully made: charred black cedar siding, fresh pale milled timber, tiny corrugated roofs, deep eaves, dry-stacked pebble footings, small salvaged glass windows. LIMITED NIGHT PALETTE: near-black, deep indigo, slate, moss green; the ONLY saturated colour is warm amber light from the windows. No text, no lettering, no signage. Looking in through the wide doorway of the tiny communal hall from outside at night. Inside, a woodstove and one hanging work-light blaze warm amber, and against that light FOUR CREATURES ARE PURE BLACK SILHOUETTES — no features at all, read entirely by posture: one perched on a table beside an open card album, two leaning together in conversation, one carrying something small across the floor. Around the doorway, giant fern fronds and grass stems arch overhead, a mushroom cap taller than the door frame, dew catching the light. Bold graphic contrast, deep black shapes against warm glow.
